desc.title: Community as JSON ("{format}", version 1)

section.usage: How the app uses this data

desc.intro:
One document describes a whole community: a tree of units (e.g. diocese → districts → circles, school → classes, retreat session → groups), positions with their rights, blueprints for similar units, people with their positions and the settings of the five steps of the guided setup. It is the same document that “Communities” → “New community” creates and that the community's JSON tab shows.
What the import does:
- First it shows a plan (a list of changes): new and moved units, roles, access, people's links, parts of areas. It saves only after “Import”.
- Unit = an area in Recreatio (under the area of the unit above). Position in a unit = a role of that area (“Animator couple · Circle 3”). Person = one personal link that holds all of their roles (a member in the circle, a leader in the district). The unit's tools (chats, calendar, pages, sign-ups) are created as an area document (“recreatio/area”) and go through the same import.
- Everything is named by keys. The community remembers what was created under which key: the same document imported again CHANGES the same things (names, place in the tree, staffing, settings) instead of duplicating them. A document from another community creates everything here anew.
- Nothing is deleted silently: a unit with "remove": true is no longer managed (the area and its content stay), a person with "remove": true loses their link. A unit or person missing from the document stays unchanged.
- Changing a person's roles (a new position, a position given up) gives them a NEW link and the old one stops working. Content stays with the position — the successor takes it over.
Return ONE JSON object, without comments.

top.name: name of the community (omitted — name of the top unit)
top.positions: positions — each described once, used in many units (below: Positions)
top.fields: person fields from step 4 (below: Person fields)
top.unit: the top unit, with its units in "units" (below: Units)
top.persons: people with their places (below: People); people can also be entered as a group in a unit's "people"

positions.key: short name (lowercase letters, digits, - and _, up to 32 characters), e.g. "para-animatorska"
positions.name: name, e.g. "Para animatorska"
positions.pair: true — filled by a couple; each of the two is a separate person with their own link, both in the same position (they write as the same role, you can see who wrote)
positions.assign: how it is filled: {words} — information for the leaders
positions.term: term in words, e.g. "3 years, +2 possible"
positions.need: how many are needed in each unit with this position (staffing: “2 missing”)
positions.per: { "count": 4, "of": "uczestnik" } — one person per this many of another position (or per this many places from "intake.limit")
positions.note: note, e.g. "elected in June; at first the pilot couple appoints for a year"

fields.label: label, e.g. "Voice"
fields.options: for "choice": a list of values, e.g. ["sopran", "alt", "tenor", "bas"]
fields.leadersOnly: true — only the leaders see it (health, diet, contact to parents)

units.key: short name (up to 40 characters), e.g. "krag-3"; omitted — from the name
units.name: name, e.g. "Circle 3"
units.kind: kind of area: {kinds}; omitted — from the blueprint or "group"
units.from: key of a blueprint from "blueprints" — the unit takes positions, settings and parts from it; changing the blueprint changes all units made from it, except what a unit set itself
units.positions: position keys of this unit (in addition to those from the blueprint)
units.settings: settings of the five steps (below: Settings); what is missing is inherited
units.council: { "key", "name", "own": [positions of this unit], "below": [positions of the units directly below] } — a council (e.g. a district circle); an area under the unit whose membership follows the staffing
units.people: { "{slot}": ["First Last", "@person-key", …] } — people as a group, e.g. all pupils of 2b; in more detail — in "persons"
units.address: address of the unit's pages, e.g. "dk/rejon-13"; omitted — address of the unit above + "/" + key (at the top: from the community name)
units.area: id of an EXISTING area that becomes this unit and is moved to this place (e.g. two districts under a new diocese) — only deliberately
units.remove: true — dissolved: the community stops managing it (removes the access it gave); the area and its content stay
units.extra: additional parts of the area document — "appointments", "pages", "subforms", "card", "category", "listings", "chats", "publish" — exactly as in the “area” format

persons.key: short name (omitted — from the full name), e.g. "anna-kowalska"
persons.name: full name — sealed in the units' areas; the service does not see it
persons.places: [{ "unit": "krag-3", "position": "czlonek" }, { "unit": "rejon-13", "position": "para-rejonowa" }] — all places of the person; membership and position are separate
persons.pair: key of the other person of the couple
persons.remove: true — the person leaves: their link stops working

desc.blueprints: Entry in "blueprints": { "key", "name", "kind", "positions", "settings", "council", "extra" } — like a unit, without "units". A unit with "from": "{slot}" takes everything from it that it does not set itself. A blueprint can also be made in the app from an existing unit (“Save as a blueprint”).
desc.usage:
- “Communities” (#/workspace/wspolnoty) shows the tree (a map to drag or a list on the phone), the settings of each unit in five steps with “inherited from …” / “set here” and “Restore inherited”, people with links, staffing (where someone is missing), JSON and the history of changes with “Restore this version”.
- Every unit's area shows “Managed by the community …” with a link; changes made there by hand may be overwritten by the next import.
- A person with a link sees only their own units: chats (with "tools.chat"), a calendar with the dates above (with "visibility.subunitsSee" above), the unit's page (“for us”), “Write to the leaders” ("tools.askLeaders").
- A council has its own chat; it includes the roles of the positions from "own" and "below" — when the staffing changes, the council changes.
- Public sign-up ("intake.mode": "signup") is on the unit's page; those who sign up get the role of the participant position (the first with the right "participant" or "member").
- The field "leadersOnly" and "intake.health" — data for the leaders only (questions in the leaders' sub-form or in the form's requirements).
- What the import does not do by itself (the setting is saved and shown in the unit with the way to the tool): lessons and materials (Scriptorium / Library, in a class — the Class tab), learning with Cogita (review modules on the unit's page), polls downwards, attendance and own tables (a form with leaders' extensions), the place limit and the waiting list (information in the form; counting places is not built).
